title: Clock
description: Where the device learns what time it is. Everything espOS publishes is UTC; the timezone below is for displays only.

keys.name: sntp
keys.title: Set the clock from NTP
keys.description: Ask an NTP server for the time once the network is up. Off = the clock comes only from the SignalK stream or a manual set, which is what a device on a boat network with no internet route wants.

keys.name: server0
keys.title: NTP server
keys.description: Host name or IP. Empty and with DHCP off, nothing is asked.

keys.name: server1
keys.title: Second NTP server
keys.description: Optional fallback, used when the first does not answer.

keys.name: from_dhcp
keys.title: Use the NTP server DHCP offers
keys.description: Many routers hand out an NTP server with the lease, and it is usually the router itself — reachable even when the boat has no internet. A DHCP-supplied server replaces the list above and is refreshed on every new lease.

keys.name: sk_fallback
keys.title: Fall back to the SignalK clock
keys.description: While the clock is unset, take the time from navigation.datetime on the SignalK stream. The server usually has GPS time, so a device with no internet route still gets a usable clock. Dropped as soon as NTP succeeds.

keys.name: tz
keys.title: Timezone (POSIX TZ)
keys.description: For displays only — nothing espOS sends is ever in local time. POSIX form, e.g. UTC0, CET-1CEST,M3.5.0,M10.5.0/3 for central Europe. Note the POSIX sign convention: the offset is west-positive, so CET (UTC+1) is written -1.
